old.name: Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres
old.hook: Dalí's own surrealist monument, built on a ruined theatre, his final resting place.
chips: Timed ticket; the Mae West room, the Rainy Taxi
old.text: Salvador Dalí was born in Figueres on 11 May 1904, and built his theatre-museum on the bombed shell of the town's old theatre — a total Surrealist environment crowned with eggs and golden bread loaves. He is buried in its crypt. The anchor of the Dalí Triangle.

old.name: Salvador Dalí House-Museum, Portlligat
old.hook: The fisherman's hut Dalí bought in 1930 and lived in for fifty years.
chips: Book the timed small-group visit well ahead
old.text: On the cove next to Cadaqués, Dalí expanded a single barraca into a labyrinthine home by buying adjacent huts, living and working here from 1930 to 1982 with Gala. The eroded schist of Cap de Creus outside is the literal landscape behind his melting forms. Entry is by small timed groups only.

old.name: Ruïnes d'Empúries
old.hook: The Greek Emporion and the Roman city beside it, on the L'Escala shore.
chips: Combined ticket with the archaeology museum
old.text: Founded around 575 BCE by Greeks from Massalia as Emporion, "the market," and occupied by Rome from 218 BCE as the bridgehead for the conquest of Hispania. The Palaiapolis at Sant Martí, the Neapolis on the mainland, and the Roman city above — walk it with the sea on one side.

old.name: Sant Pere de Rodes
old.hook: The Benedictine monastery on the Verdera slope that kept the vines alive.
chips: Combine with a hike up the Verdera massif
old.text: A great Romanesque monastery on the mountainside above the Gulf of Roses, a key medieval landholder that carried Empordà viticulture through the Middle Ages. The view from its terrace runs the length of the coast to Cap de Creus.

old_also.name: The terrace of Sant Pere de Rodes
old_also.text: From the monastery forecourt the coast unrolls to Cap de Creus; the wind, the Romanesque stone, and almost nobody out of season.

old.name: Santa Maria de Castelló d'Empúries
old.hook: The "Cathedral of l'Empordà" — a Gothic church in a former county capital.
chips: The carved alabaster retable and the tower
old.text: Rebuilt in Gothic style in the late thirteenth century and so grand for a small town that locals call it the Cathedral of l'Empordà, it marks Castelló d'Empúries' centuries as seat of the Counts of Empúries. Often overlooked by visitors heading straight for the coast.

old.name: Cap de Creus Natural Park
old.hook: The easternmost point of Iberia, where the Pyrenees plunge into the sea.
chips: Drive or walk to the Cap de Creus lighthouse
Open access; visitor centre at Palau de Tudela
old.text: About 14,000 hectares of Precambrian schist 580–540 million years old, folded by the Variscan orogeny into the contorted shear zones of the Paratge de Tudela — the wind- and sea-sculpted rock that fed Dalí's imagery. A geological textbook with a lighthouse at the tip.

old.name: elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi (Roses)
old.hook: Ferran Adrià's legendary restaurant, reopened as a museum in 2023.
chips: Book the timed visit; the access road is rough
Seasonal (roughly half the year); reserve online
old.text: The cove above Roses where elBulli was five times the world's best restaurant is now a museum of creativity — 69 multimedia installations across some 4,000 m², named for the 1,846 dishes the team created. It runs as a six-month museum and becomes the elBulliDNA research lab off-season.
